rule: A source-driven parent preserves the interleaving of connected text and element children.
synthetic_input: Map text and b children of a paragraph containing A, b(B), C.
expected: The content order is A, b(B), C; collecting text first would change it.

rule: Processing instructions and comments have separate inclusion settings on a mixed-content connection.
synthetic_input: Include comments but leave processing instructions off; input has one of each.
expected: The comment is eligible for copying; selecting it does not also select the instruction.

rule: Auto-connect can relax role, case, namespace and punctuation comparisons.
synthetic_input: Use role mixing on source attribute code and target element code, with compatible types.
expected: The attribute/element difference does not itself exclude this match.

rule: A manual copy-all on partially matching structures covers compatible children.
synthetic_input: Source has name:string and size:int; target has name:string and size:date.
expected: name can participate; the incompatible size does not become a conversion by connecting the parents.

rule: Copy-all between a schema and a user-function parameter requires the same schema, but not the same root.
synthetic_input: Use two roots declared by one XSD for component and parameter.
expected: Different roots alone do not violate the documented schema-identity requirement.

rule: Source-driven connections can carry comments and processing instructions. Connection annotations are labels.
synthetic_input: Label a connection keep-comments without enabling comment mapping.
expected: The label does not enable copying comments.

rule: Inserting a filter on an existing connection puts that component between the selected source and target.
synthetic_input: Insert a filter on the entries-to-rows line in a mapping with another independent target.
expected: The edited path includes the filter; the independent target path is unaffected.

rule: Moving a broken parent connection after a root change offers an option to move matching descendant connections too.
synthetic_input: Rename a root while retaining its connected child code. Move the parent connection and include descendants.
expected: The matching code connection can move with its parent; this is not a remap of every old child.

rule: Smart deletion is off by default. Deleting a processing component then deletes its direct connections.
synthetic_input: Delete a filter in a source → filter → target path using the default setting.
expected: The two direct connections disappear; no bypass is implied.

rule: Preview for C++, C# or Java uses the built-in engine. Output validation is a separate, schema-dependent action.
synthetic_input: Select Java, preview an XML target, then validate the output.
expected: The preview supplies XML for validation; neither action demonstrates execution of compiled Java.

rule: The generated-code option for absolute component paths excludes external libraries. Generated XSLT/XQuery has a separate library-reference setting.
synthetic_input: Choose absolute component paths and library references relative to the generated XSLT.
expected: The library reference can remain relative while a component path becomes absolute.

rule: An ordinary repeating target gets no occurrence from an empty sequence.
synthetic_input: Feed [] into repeating XML reading elements.
expected: There are zero reading elements, not one empty-string element.

rule: A repeating sequence can drive multiple target rows, but a simple output accepts only one item.
synthetic_input: Send [7,8,9] separately to an ordinary repeating row and a simple output.
expected: The row target can contain three occurrences; the simple output returns one value.

rule: An XML document root is created only once. The documented sequence-to-root case with connected root attributes fails serialization.
synthetic_input: Connect two source items to an XML root and connect a root attribute too.
expected: Expect a runtime serialization failure rather than two document roots.

rule: Independent sequence inputs to a multi-input function can produce combinations rather than positional pairs.
synthetic_input: Supply [A,B] and [1,2,3] as independent arguments to concatenation.
expected: There are six combinations, not two zipped values; no order assumption is necessary.

rule: Ordinary non-sequence functions propagate absence. Existence tests and aggregates are documented exceptions.
synthetic_input: Supply an empty sequence separately to an ordinary unary string transformation, exists, and count.
expected: The ordinary result is absent; the latter two give false and 0.

rule: Restricting a parent connection restricts the source data visible to target descendants.
synthetic_input: Keep only station North before creating target stations. North owns probes N1,N2; South owns S1.
expected: North's target children see N1,N2, not S1.

rule: Child-field feeds need not create one parent per source record. The illustrated unwired-parent shape yields one parent with repeated child values and a warning.
synthetic_input: Omit the parent-to-parent connection in that shape; two records each have a code.
expected: The two codes can land under one target parent. Connecting parents supplies the missing iteration.

rule: Connecting an aggregate's parent context changes its grouping and can change its result cardinality.
synthetic_input: Two batches have 2 and 3 samples. Count under a common parent, then per batch with corresponding target rows.
expected: The first count is 5; the second mapping produces counts 2 and 3.

rule: Prioritizing a comparison input can determine which candidate record's fields remain in context after a filter match.
synthetic_input: Compare requested Q with catalog parts P and Q. Give the catalog input priority in the documented two-source filter shape.
expected: The matched row takes Q's identifier and details, not identifiers from both catalog candidates.

rule: Preview selects one target. Server or generated execution processes all targets sequentially.
synthetic_input: Select manifest for preview in a design that also writes totals.
expected: The preview shows manifest; selecting it does not remove totals from multi-target execution.

rule: For ordering, a chain is one unit; moving the intermediate component within it does not order separate chains.
synthetic_input: Move only the intermediate component of chain A, keeping both final targets fixed.
expected: The move does not change the processing order between A and B.

rule: Simple input names have a restricted alphabet.
synthetic_input: Try batch_no and batch-no as parameter names.
expected: The underscore satisfies the naming rule; the hyphen does not.

rule: A mapping input defaults to string; choosing another datatype requests a cast at execution.
synthetic_input: Pass lexical 007 to an ordinary default input and to one configured as integer.
expected: The first is text 007; the second is integer 7.

rule: A required input must be supplied. A preview-only value does not become a deployment default.
synthetic_input: Set a required parameter's preview value to demo; invoke the generated mapping without the parameter.
expected: The preview value does not satisfy the required parameter for that invocation.

rule: A specified preview value overrides a connected optional default for design-time execution.
synthetic_input: Connect constant east as default, specify west for preview, and omit the value at runtime.
expected: Preview uses west; the runtime fallback is east. A required setting on a defaulted input warrants a validation warning (p.140).

rule: Input and output file names can be supplied independently through parameters with connected defaults.
synthetic_input: Default source and target to in.xml and out.xml; supply new.xml for the target only.
expected: The selected source remains in.xml; the target name changes to new.xml.

rule: Separate simple outputs expose individual results from a shared input.
synthetic_input: Feed “red fox” to string-length, substring-before(space), and substring-after(space), each wired to its own output.
expected: The three previews show 7, red, and fox respectively.

rule: Occurrence-based input optimization can process a required singleton atomically. Invalid input can yield an empty sequence and stop the mapping.
synthetic_input: A schema requires one code, but the input omits it. Compare processing with the optimization enabled and disabled.
expected: The optimized assumption can fail on absence. Disabling it permits processing invalid input without guaranteeing downstream success.

rule: Selecting a derived XML type creates a distinct source view; the instance identifies the type with xsi:type (p.156).
synthetic_input: Map only the Staff view of base Contact to badges. The input has one Staff and one Guest.
expected: Only Staff qualifies on that connection; shared base fields do not select Guest.

rule: A nil XML element exists even though it has no content.
synthetic_input: Test an explicitly nil nillable element and an absent optional element with exists.
expected: The nil element is present; the absent one is not.

rule: A database NULL normally leaves the target XML element absent. Explicit nil substitution plus a nillable target can emit the element instead.
synthetic_input: Map a NULL note directly to one optional XML target and via nil substitution to a second nillable target.
expected: The first omits note; the second emits note marked nil.

rule: One comment can be added before and one after a target node; duplicate inputs support additional comments.
synthetic_input: Request two separate comments before the same ordinarily connected target node.
expected: Use the duplicate-input facility rather than expecting unlimited comment ports on that node.

rule: A CDATA target emits character data; the editor warns about the section-closing delimiter.
synthetic_input: Map text <rate> to a CDATA target, then consider text containing ]]>.
expected: The first is markup-looking text, not a nested element. The page warns about the second; it does not promise automatic escaping.

rule: A wrapper includes the original and imported schemas without overwriting the original. A schema opened from a URL cannot be edited in place.
synthetic_input: Extend wildcard selections for a remote schema using a separate local schema.
expected: Generate a wrapper rather than editing the remote schema; the component can use the wrapper.

rule: Adding a custom target namespace exposes a pair of inputs. Both require connections even when a value is empty.
synthetic_input: On a target element, connect urn:station to namespace and an empty string to prefix.
expected: This declares a default namespace (p.168); leaving prefix unconnected is a different configuration.

rule: Stripping schema names applies to generated SELECT statements; it does not rewrite a manually entered statement.
synthetic_input: Enable stripping and supply a custom SELECT over reporting.measure.
expected: The setting does not remove reporting from the authored query.

rule: Connection sharing among components using the same data source is disabled by default and is not supported inside UDFs.
synthetic_input: Two components point at the same database. Leave their sharing option untouched.
expected: A common database name alone does not request a shared connection.

rule: Calculated expressions in custom SELECT statements need distinct aliases to become mappable fields.
synthetic_input: Select mass*factor AS corrected_mass and count*factor AS corrected_count.
expected: The two aliases identify separate output fields; do not infer usable field names from the formulas alone.

rule: A mapping can declare a local relationship between compatible columns even without a database foreign-key declaration.
synthetic_input: Relate a numeric bin ID in one table to a compatible bin ID in another and save the mapping.
expected: The relationship is part of the mapping; this does not require adding a constraint to the physical database.

rule: A null test, substitution and explicitly assigning database NULL are distinct operations.
synthetic_input: For a missing note, compare mapping the text “NULL” to a text column with using set-null for the column.
expected: The string is a literal value; explicit NULL assignment requests a database null.

rule: An external read in a per-item UDF context can be evaluated repeatedly. An eligible join or combined query can reduce unnecessary calls.
synthetic_input: Pass four IDs individually to a scalar-parameter UDF containing a database read.
expected: The mapping can demand four reads. Reusing identical connection settings does not make the call compute once.

rule: Table actions run in order. Actions after Insert All or Insert Rest cannot run; the editor flags the unreachable action.
synthetic_input: Put Update If by key before Insert Rest. Supply one existing key and one absent key.
expected: The matching row takes the update; the unmatched row takes the insert. A later Delete If would not get another opportunity.

rule: For numeric columns without autoincrement, max()+1 derives the next value from existing values. DB-generated is a separate option for an autoincrement key.
synthetic_input: A non-autoincrement target contains keys 1,3,8. Request max()+1 for a new record.
expected: The candidate value is 9. This does not establish concurrent-insert safety.

rule: In the illustrated parent/child Insert All configuration, the parent key is DB-generated and supplied to the related child foreign key.
synthetic_input: One new parent receives ID 21 and owns two new children. Map the children's other columns but not the parent ID.
expected: In that relationship both child rows receive 21 as parent key; each child's generated primary key is separate.

rule: With current-transaction-and-continue enabled only at the parent, the parent and its children form an atomic unit.
synthetic_input: A has two children; one violates a constraint. B and its children are valid.
expected: Roll back A and both its children; processing continues with B.

rule: With transaction handling only on the child, top and current coincide at that level in the illustrated failure.
synthetic_input: Enable current-and-continue on children alone. The parent is valid; its first child succeeds and its second fails.
expected: The failing child is rolled back. That child error does not automatically undo the whole family.

rule: In an eligible hierarchical update, generated MERGE is confined to the deepest mapped child table. The page uses both “Insert If” and “Update If” when describing eligibility; their equivalence is unresolved.
synthetic_input: Inspect an otherwise eligible two-level parent/child update.
expected: Do not expect MERGE at both levels. Parent UPDATE output is consistent with the documented hierarchy rule.

rule: The source view of a procedure is for retrieving data without supplying input parameters; a parameterized call uses a different representation.
synthetic_input: A routine needs an input batch number before it can return rows.
expected: Select a call with parameters rather than relying on the parameterless source view.

rule: A procedure call can expose input, output and return parameters as well as a recordset; the recordset structure must be described for mapping.
synthetic_input: A procedure returns a status plus rows of (id,weight). Configure only the status port.
expected: The status is not a declaration of the two row fields; supply the recordset structure to wire those fields.

rule: Duplicating a stored procedure's target input creates separate calls for the duplicated inputs.
synthetic_input: Wire two independently populated duplicate inputs of a target procedure.
expected: Expect a call per populated duplicate in the described setup, not one combined invocation.

rule: A local relationship can arrange dependent target procedure calls hierarchically, with the primary-key object as parent.
synthetic_input: A parent procedure creates an ID and a related procedure consumes it to insert details.
expected: The generated ID can supply the child call; unrelated visual adjacency is not the relationship.

rule: The preview of a database update reports pseudo-SQL. Transactions appear as hints, while actual transaction commands go to the database API during execution.
synthetic_input: Preview an update with transaction handling enabled.
expected: Comments indicating a transaction are expected; their presence does not demonstrate a committed insert.

rule: The NoSQL query pane can list collections without supporting query execution. Filtering via the WHERE/ORDER component is a separate facility.
synthetic_input: Browse a MongoDB collection and try to infer query-pane execution from the visible collection name.
expected: The visible name confirms discovery only; use the supported mapping filter for record selection.

rule: The NoSQL component workflow requires built-in transformation language and an assigned schema.
synthetic_input: Configure a MongoDB collection, then request the same mapping as generated Java.
expected: The documented component workflow does not qualify that Java route.

rule: X12/HIPAA validation exposes message and group parser errors for acknowledgment mappings. The creation command is limited to these component types (p.478).
synthetic_input: Build an acknowledgment from a group containing a faulty transaction.
expected: Use the appropriate group and message diagnostics rather than treating every error as interchange-wide.

rule: The documented CONTRL creation facility applies to standard EDIFACT messages.
synthetic_input: Choose between a standard and an interactive EDIFACT component when authoring an acknowledgment.
expected: The existence of the standard-message facility does not make it available for the interactive case.

rule: For fields configured for incomplete validation, a code not in the supplied list can warn and continue rather than stopping the mapping.
synthetic_input: An externally defined code is not present in a field's incomplete local copy of the list.
expected: Continued processing is documented; it does not certify that the external code is correct.

rule: Full global checking of a previously incomplete field requires enabling full validation and including the external values in the code lists.
synthetic_input: Enable full checking while omitting an external code used by a sender.
expected: The field is now checked against the configured full set; toggling the flag does not import the missing code.

rule: A message-specific list can restrict a shared field. Where a global list also exists, local values must occur globally; the configured invalid-code action affects the outcome.
synthetic_input: Global codes are A,B; a message admits A,C locally.
expected: C creates a validation conflict. A local list alone does not waive the global restriction.

rule: Character-list tests use positive one-based offsets and lengths. Tests in one named list are conjunctive; alternative lists provide alternative ways to pass.
synthetic_input: For one list require position 1 in {A,B} and positions 2–3 equal 07. Supply A08.
expected: The first condition passes but the list fails. With no other matching list the field is invalid.

rule: Standard EDIFACT validation compares the message reference in UNH and UNT as well as checking the pair.
synthetic_input: Supply a header reference 17 and trailer reference 18 with both segments present.
expected: Presence of the pair does not satisfy the reference equality check.

rule: For standard EDIFACT output UNA is written at the start unless suppression is selected.
synthetic_input: Generate otherwise identical standard interchanges with and without Suppress UNA.
expected: The default case has UNA. The suppressed case omits that segment; the checkbox is not a change of message type.

rule: The documented older configuration upgrade changes the message node identity. An open mapping must reload to pick up the revised connections.
synthetic_input: Upgrade the illustrated old ORDERS configuration while its design is open.
expected: Reload the design; do not infer that editing the file alone refreshed the open node tree.

rule: A message configuration's Include references must identify files in the same directory.
synthetic_input: Add an Include for a segment dictionary present only in an unrelated directory.
expected: The existence of a file of that name elsewhere does not meet the documented configuration requirement.

rule: A data element defaults to one required occurrence. Setting minOccurs to zero makes it optional.
synthetic_input: Declare two fields and put minOccurs=0 only on the second.
expected: Omitting the second meets its lower bound; omitting the first does not.

rule: A merged data element can expose several consecutive wire positions as one repeating mapping node. Separate named nodes can instead give positions distinct meanings (p.504).
synthetic_input: Set mergedEntries=2 and receive values North and South in the two positions.
expected: One mapped source node supplies two occurrences to a repeating target, rather than two independently named fields.

rule: A HIPAA configuration can hide an otherwise optional field with maxOccurs=0; the hidden item cannot be mapped as a target.
synthetic_input: Leave the zero bound on a field while other fields in its segment are mapped.
expected: That field has no target output merely because the segment itself is generated.

rule: Quick EDI-to-XML conversion derives XML from the source data. Empty fields are omitted and the generated structure cannot be customized in that mode.
synthetic_input: Convert one record with a populated label and a second with that field empty.
expected: Do not expect an empty label element solely to match the first record's shape.

rule: Creating a variable from a target node gives it that target structure and automatically connects the items using copy-all.
synthetic_input: Create a variable from the input connector of a target reading with children id and value.
expected: The new variable starts with the reading schema and a copy-all connection rather than two newly designed scalar parameters.

rule: An unconnected compute-when evaluates on first use in a target subtree and shares the result with descendants; unrelated target uses can evaluate separately.
synthetic_input: Two siblings below the same target row use a variable. A different target subtree also uses it.
expected: The siblings share the row's evaluation; do not treat the unrelated use as sharing that evaluation.

rule: Compute Once is scoped per target component; within a UDF it is per function invocation.
synthetic_input: Invoke the same UDF for three independent records. It contains a Compute Once variable.
expected: Once in the function does not mean once for all three invocations.

rule: A count reused on each output person can be placed in a Compute Once variable to avoid recounting the database table for each record.
synthetic_input: One output target writes four labels, each including the count of a six-row reference table.
expected: All four labels can reuse 6; the intended count evaluation is once for the target.

rule: Numbering the variable that receives accepted nodes numbers the filtered sequence, not the original input.
synthetic_input: Keep source records at positions 2 and 5 and send the filter output into the variable before taking position.
expected: The two retained records get IDs 1 and 2, not 2 and 5.

rule: Grouping by a key before splitting into fixed-size blocks makes the block number relative to that key.
synthetic_input: Set block size to 2. Key A has five records and B has three. Build one distinct filename per key and block.
expected: A has blocks of 2,2,1 and B of 2,1: five files overall. B's numbering starts at its own first block.

rule: Multiple join conditions are conjunctive, including an optional condition added on the mapping.
synthetic_input: The property condition requires matching station and the mapped condition requires active=true. A candidate matches the station but is inactive.
expected: That candidate does not contribute a joined pair.

rule: A new join has two inputs. More can be added; removal cannot leave fewer than two.
synthetic_input: Add a third structure then remove it.
expected: The two-structure join remains; removing another input is unavailable in this state.

rule: Joining XML records on two fields rejects partial key matches.
synthetic_input: Compare (dock,shift) against (A,day), (A,night), and (B,day), with required key (A,day).
expected: Only the first pair qualifies; comparing dock alone would admit the night record.

locator: Both objects that are to be joined must originate
rule: SQL-mode join eligibility requires the same database and component, conditions defined in properties, and no joined table already in target-parent context.
synthetic_input: Use the same database in two distinct mapping components, one table per component.
expected: Being on the same database alone does not establish SQL-mode eligibility.

rule: In SQL mode the topmost table is the left side of a left outer join.
synthetic_input: Left keys are [A,B] and the right table has a single A. Compare an inner join with a left outer join.
expected: The inner result includes A alone; the left outer result also retains B without a matching right row.

rule: In the illustrated SQL join the editor derives equality from a detected foreign key when the tables are wired through their parent-child relationship.
synthetic_input: A parent key 5 has child foreign keys [5,7]. Use the detected relationship in an inner join.
expected: The child with 5 matches. Showing two independent top-level tables does not guarantee the same automatic condition.

rule: When configuring a later join input, its condition can use fields from structures preceding it, not just its immediate predecessor.
synthetic_input: Join line→order on order ID. Add product as input three and compare its ID to the product ID from line.
expected: The third comparison may reference input one; it need not compare an order field to product ID.

rule: Key position sets comparison priority, and each key has its own direction.
synthetic_input: Sort (2,B), (1,Z), (2,A) by descending number then ascending letter.
expected: The result is (2,A), (2,B), (1,Z). No exact-tie stability rule is needed.

rule: An intermediate variable can capture ancestor information with each record before sorting across parents.
synthetic_input: Capture (Z,west) and (A,east), then sort globally by the name in the captured record.
expected: Output starts with (A,east); the sorted record keeps its original parent information.

rule: With only the true output wired, the current node passes on a true condition; a false condition emits no node on that path.
synthetic_input: Rows have flags [false,true,false,true]. Connect the true branch to a repeating target row.
expected: The second and fourth rows contribute two target occurrences.

rule: A scalar if-else with no matching condition and an unconnected otherwise produces no result.
synthetic_input: Test x<0 and x>10; connect the result to an optional attribute. Inputs are -1, 0, 10, 11.
expected: The attribute appears for -1 and 11 and is absent at both boundaries; it is not an empty attribute.

rule: Accepting a WHERE clause triggers validation of the resulting SQL; an optional ORDER BY can use comma-separated keys (p.739).
synthetic_input: Enter a syntactically incomplete predicate and confirm the dialog.
expected: The editor prompts on the invalid statement instead of treating the missing expression as an unconditional match.

rule: Set a lookup column to Boolean when it is driven by a Boolean result. The otherwise branch can supply a distinct value.
synthetic_input: Use true→review and otherwise→skip; feed an actual Boolean true followed by false.
expected: The outputs are review and skip. The example does not require comparing the input to text "true".

rule: An unconfigured Otherwise yields an empty result on a lookup miss, which can omit an XML target element.
synthetic_input: Map N→new with no fallback. Process source codes N and Q.
expected: The first gets new; the second has no mapped value. Preserving Q requires an explicit fallback.

rule: The first-match policy executes only the earliest matching rule.
synthetic_input: Order rules amount>10→review then amount>20→hold. Input amount is 25.
expected: Only review is produced, even though both predicates are true.

rule: The all-match policy emits the actions of all matching rules as a sequence.
synthetic_input: Use the same ordered rules and amount 25 with all-match selected.
expected: The matching actions are review and hold, rather than just review.

rule: An exception can be driven by a filter branch, with separately mapped error text. Equality at the strict threshold must follow the correct branch.
synthetic_input: Pass amounts below 12; connect the false branch to throw with text over-limit. Inputs tested separately are 11 and 12.
expected: 11 passes. 12 triggers over-limit, even though it is not greater than 12.

rule: An optional field can be schema-valid yet mandatory to the mapping; the not-present branch can drive an exception.
synthetic_input: Require an optional sequence-number attribute on each message by testing existence. A message lacks the attribute.
expected: The mapping's exception branch receives that message and its configured text. A schema error is not required.

rule: Function lookup searches names and description text by default. That second source can be disabled.
synthetic_input: A search term appears in a function description but not its name.
expected: The function can appear under the default search and disappear when description search is disabled.

rule: For a name collision, the main mapping precedes a locally imported function, which precedes a globally imported function.
synthetic_input: Three functions named label would return main, local, and global respectively.
expected: Calling label resolves to main. Removing the main definition allows the local import to win over global.

rule: A locally imported library can be referenced relative to the design; a global import path stays absolute.
synthetic_input: Move a directory containing a mapping and its locally imported sibling library together.
expected: Their relative reference can survive the move. The same option cannot make a global import relative.

rule: Defaults and node functions do not apply to descendants under a copy-all connection. A simple-valued parent can itself have a rule.
synthetic_input: Attach an inherited string rule above a copied subtree and expect each copied descendant to gain a suffix.
expected: That descendant transformation is outside the documented copy-all rule scope.

rule: For a default rule, leaving its value field empty specifies the empty string.
synthetic_input: Define a string default and deliberately leave the rule value empty.
expected: The rule has a string value of length zero; an empty editor field does not by itself mean no rule exists.

rule: A field may override an inherited default or block inheritance without setting a replacement (p.777).
synthetic_input: An ancestor's numeric default is 5; give one empty child a local default 9 and block inheritance at another empty child.
expected: The first uses 9; the second does not acquire 5 solely from the ancestor.

rule: Defaults can apply to unconnected target nodes if a parent or sibling is connected. The manual explicitly excludes unconnected JSON nodes.
synthetic_input: An unconnected text target field has default pending and its parent is connected. Compare the illustrated tabular target with an unconnected JSON property.
expected: The former can acquire pending. The latter does not acquire it through this rule.

rule: When metadata does not apply to a node, the function can be skipped or supplied an empty sequence. The latter may need an explicit fallback.
synthetic_input: Select a length facet on a node that has none; configure missing metadata to produce an empty sequence, then substitute “unknown”.
expected: The function can produce unknown. Selecting skip instead bypasses the node function rather than supplying that fallback.

locator: Regular functions can have only one output
rule: Inline functions can have multiple outputs but cannot recurse. Regular functions can recurse and have one output, which may be structured.
synthetic_input: Design a recursive tree walk that returns a node name and depth.
expected: Use a regular function with one structured result; multiple inline outputs do not enable recursion.

rule: A regular sequence parameter receives the whole sequence in one call. A non-sequence input causes one call per item, and none on an empty sequence.
synthetic_input: Feed [2,8] and [] to a regular count function under both parameter settings.
expected: Sequence input gives one call with [2,8] and one with []; scalar input gives two calls for the pair and none for [].

rule: Output cardinality is independent of input cardinality. With sequence output disabled a multi-item result is truncated.
synthetic_input: The function body supplies [red,blue] to its output.
expected: With scalar output it returns red alone; enabling sequence output permits both values.

rule: A regular UDF can process child directories recursively and filter file names while preserving the directory hierarchy.
synthetic_input: Directory root contains a.txt and child dir sub containing b.xml. Select names containing .xml.
expected: sub and b.xml remain nested under root; a.txt is not selected.

rule: One sequence-parameter UDF call does not limit the number of requests made by a service inside the function.
synthetic_input: Invoke once with quantities [2,3]. Compare wiring both items to Request with wiring their single sum to Request.
expected: The first can drive multiple requests inside the single invocation; the second can issue one with 5 if the aggregate's parent context is singular.

rule: The illustrated lookup compares several supplied key values before a filter releases a candidate's details.
synthetic_input: Two stations share contact Ada Lane but differ in office code. Supply office W, Ada, Lane as the three key values.
expected: Only W's matching details pass; comparing the name alone would mix the two offices.

rule: Per-item file naming can combine a source field, sequential number and constant extension.
synthetic_input: Two consecutive input records both carry category tide. Start numbering at 1 and build category+number+.xml.
expected: The names are tide1.xml and tide2.xml; the shared category need not collapse the records into one file.

rule: One unique row key can determine one document name per database record.
synthetic_input: Rows have distinct keys 17 and 23. Send key plus .xml to the target's dynamic filename port.
expected: The resulting document set has names 17.xml and 23.xml. No row order is inferred.

rule: One string adapter cannot both consume a serialized string and produce a serialized string at the same time.
synthetic_input: Wire both directions at the root of a single adapter.
expected: The manual specifies an error. Use distinct parser and serializer components for a two-stage transformation.

rule: Declaring a fixed-width field integer validates its extracted text numerically; declaring field widths alone does not supply that type.
synthetic_input: One fixed-width string contains a three-character numeric field. Compare 042 with BAD in that field.
expected: 042 is a valid integer lexical value; BAD does not satisfy the numeric check. Exact diagnostic text is unspecified.

rule: To serialize a selected XML element as the document root, the root-selection dialog lists global declarations, not local ones.
synthetic_input: Person is globally declared; nickname is only local. Choose a root before sending the serialized XML to a database text column.
expected: Person is selectable as the root; nickname is not offered merely because it appears below Person.
